result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers are well structured and treat each page as a landing page. B gives getting started and the changelog their own top-level places, adds an owner and a separate list of states to the template, and includes a searchable token table. B also suits a two-person team better: it adds patterns only after a second team needs them and puts placeholder pages on undocumented components. A buries the changelog under Contributing and lists getting started fifth, though it has good advice on search synonyms and stable URLs. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give concrete navigation, a strong component template, and search and deep-link advice. A does better on the rubric's specifics. It gives Changelog its own top-level nav item and adds a searchable token reference. Its template includes an owner, it treats states as a separate section, and it defers work explicitly: patterns wait until a second team needs one, and unported components get stub pages. B's ordering suits lookups well, but it folds the changelog into Contributing, leaves ownership off the template, and presents patterns as core work instead of something to defer.
